patient_information: A 55-year-old Swiss couple, both fitness instructors, travelled for 3 months from Ecuador to Chile.
chief_complaint: The husband presented with fever, myalgias, generalized weakness, and shortness of breath with oxygen desaturation; the wife presented 3 weeks later with similar complaints.
history_of_present_illness: The husband developed fever, myalgias, and weakness on the flight back to Switzerland, presenting 4 days later with ongoing symptoms, oxygen desaturation, and bilateral interstitial infiltrates, requiring non-invasive ventilator support. His wife presented 3 weeks later with similar complaints, rapidly deteriorated, developed cardiorespiratory failure, multi-organ failure, profuse bleeding, and required mass transfusions.
exposure_and_epidemiology: They spent the last month of their trip hiking, camping, and taking occasional mud baths in the Chile-Argentinian border region, an area endemic for Andesvirus.
vitals: Husband on admission: BP 90/55 mmHg, pulse 120 bpm, O2 saturation 94% on ambient air, temperature 39°C (102.2°F). Wife on admission: normal BP, normal heart rate, normal O2 saturation, temperature 38.6°C (101.5°F).
physical_exam: Husband on admission: No abnormal findings on cardiopulmonary auscultation. Wife on admission: No abnormal findings on auscultation.
labs_and_diagnostics: Husband on admission: WCC 7.3 G/L, 35% band neutrophils, platelets 48 G/L, CRP 68 mg/L, GFR >90 mL/min, normal transaminases. Wife on admission: WCC 1.88 G/L, platelets 98 G/L, CRP 7 mg/L, GFR >90 mL/min, normal transaminases. Chest x-ray showed bilateral interstitial infiltrates for the husband at presentation and for the wife during her disease course; initial chest radiography was normal for both patients. Respiratory pathogen panel and HIV test were negative for the husband.
differential_diagnosis: Differential diagnoses included influenza and other respiratory viruses, New World hantaviruses, pneumococcal pneumonia, Rickettsial diseases (Rickettsia rickettsiae, scrub typhus), pulmonary plague, fungal infections (Histoplasmosis, Cryptococcosis), severe malaria, and most viral haemorrhagic fevers.
management_and_clinical_course: Both patients were referred to a tertiary care setting for ARDS and hemorrhagic fevers, receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics and requiring standard hygiene and droplet precautions. The husband was treated with non-invasive ventilation for 5 days and made a full recovery after a month of rehabilitation. The wife required nearly a full month on ECMO, renal replacement therapy, mass blood product transfusions, multiple surgical interventions for bleeding complications, and remained in intensive care for 5 months, followed by 12 months in rehabilitation.
final_diagnosis: Both patients were confirmed by PCR and serology to be infected with Andesvirus (ANDV), a New World species of the family Hantaviridae.
